text: Hey everybody, Anthony Alfredo here and
time for a new Logitech G track lap with
Fast Pasta. This time we're at the Iowa
Speedway on iRacing. This was recently
updated
as the track was re-scanned and first of
all, they did a phenomenal job. iRacing
always kills it
with these updates, but
it is exactly like what I remember
racing here last year and it's uh going
to provide great
training opportunity for me this
weekend. So, as you see, they re-paved
the corners here, but not the
straightaways and not even the entire
corner, just the first two lanes and
then there's like an added third lane on
exit that you sort of drive into. The
interesting part is you're sliding into
the corner with not a lot of grip and
then you hit the new pavement and all of
a sudden the car grips back up. You can
kind of aim for that third lane patch on
exit to carry that grip a little bit
longer,
but if you get too high, you're going to
be up out of that. So, you got to stay
on the new pavement in the corner and
then actually pedal the car a little bit
transitioning off of it to the new
pavement because it's got a lot less
grip obviously. So, it's really unique.
It's unlike a lot of other tracks. And
I'm kind of running this middle lane
just trying to carry my momentum, but
we'll work the bottom lane here because
that is better especially on fresher
tires. You just got to get down to this
white line, tip into the throttle slowly
and come off low and straight. You'll
actually straddle that top
lane of new pavement and the old
pavement. You'll see
kind of where I aim on exit. That's a
good point to come off low and straight
right there
and you can get your hands straight. Try
not to hit the wall
and carry the most momentum up off the
corner without over slipping the front
or the rear tires. So, this is a really
cool track. It used to be super rough.
Obviously, where they re-paved it's a
lot smoother now,
but unfortunately, you know, you used to
run all four or five lanes, be up here
by the wall, but it's just not possible
anymore. It's all dirty. There's way
less grip, and you're just not going to
be up there. So, got to stay on the dark
black fresh pavement to make the most
out of your race and carry the the most
amount of speed because it's just got so
much more grip. It's way faster, and you
can set up passes in that second lane,
so it's still pretty racy. It's still a
fun track,
but a lot different than the old Iowa
Speedway
we always knew. So, hopefully some of
these tips help you out this week,
and I look forward to seeing how you do
in your fixed races.
Be back with another track lap next
week, and hopefully I catch you in an
official lobby this week on iRacing.
